title: Gantt Chart Period Label Selection Guide: Week vs Month vs Quarter
content:
Gantt Chart Period Label Selection Guide

The period label (Week, Month, or Quarter) determines the column unit on a Gantt chart. Choosing the wrong unit makes the chart unreadable. Always calculate total project duration first, then apply this rule.

## Decision Table

| Total Project Duration | Period Label | Column Unit | Typical Column Count |
|---|---|---|---|
| Less than 6 months | Week | 1 week per column | 4–24 columns |
| 6 to 18 months | Month | 1 month per column | 6–18 columns |
| More than 18 months | Quarter | 3 months per column | 7–20 columns |

## Why This Matters
- A 44-month project rendered in monthly columns = 44 tiny, unreadable columns
- A 44-month project rendered in quarterly columns = 15 readable columns
- Optimal column count for readability: 8–20 columns
- More than 24 columns on a Gantt = unreadable, even in landscape

## Calculation Method
1. Find the earliest task start and latest task end (in months)
2. Total duration = max(end months) - min(start months) + 1
3. Apply the decision table above
4. If using Quarters: convert all task start/end from months to quarters using ceil(month / 3)

## Examples
- Project Month 1 to Month 5 → 5 months → use WEEKS (e.g., Week 1 to Week 20)
- Project Month 1 to Month 12 → 12 months → use MONTHS (Month 1 to Month 12)
- Project Month 1 to Month 18 → 18 months → use MONTHS (Month 1 to Month 18)
- Project Month 1 to Month 19 → 19 months → use QUARTERS (Q1 to Q7)
- Project Month 1 to Month 44 → 44 months → use QUARTERS (Q1 to Q15)
- Project Month 1 to Month 36 → 36 months → use QUARTERS (Q1 to Q12)

## Task Date Rescaling for Quarters
When switching to Quarter period label, rescale all task start/end values:
- Quarter number = ceiling(month_number / 3)
- Month 1 → Q1, Month 2 → Q1, Month 3 → Q1
- Month 4 → Q2, Month 5 → Q2, Month 6 → Q2
- Month 7 → Q3 ... and so on
- Task duration in quarters = end_quarter - start_quarter + 1

## Most Common Mistake
Using 'Month' as the period label for projects longer than 18 months. This is always wrong. A 2–4 year project must use Quarters. A 5+ year project may use Quarters or even Half-Years.

## Landscape vs Portrait
- Up to 16 period columns: portrait orientation is acceptable
- More than 16 period columns: switch to landscape orientation for readability
- With Quarter label and 15 columns: landscape is strongly recommended
